transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. It's good to meet you too. 

Well, I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I just can’t seem to organize all the moving parts in my life anymore. There's a lot on my plate right now—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions at work—and I just... I can't keep it all straight. 

Instead of figuring out what needs to be done first, I just end up starting on whatever is loudest at the moment, instead of what actually matters. It's getting really frustrating.
Have you had this kind of trouble organizing tasks and prioritizing what matters since you were a child?

Yeah, looking back, it definitely was. Even back in grade school, long before I was a teenager. 

My teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but that I daydreamed a lot. I would actually finish my assignments and then just... forget to turn them in. Or I'd completely lose my homework folders. So, yes, it's been an issue for a very long time.
Do these problems with organization and follow-through affect you in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home?

Yeah, definitely. It's... it's not just at work. Like I mentioned earlier with the gallery deadlines and the workshop prep, that's all my own stuff at home. And then at my job, it's the exact same issue with trying to manage team decisions and my regular tasks. So, yeah, it pretty much spills over into every part of my life right now.
Have there been times when your trouble staying organized completely went away while your mood was normal?

No, I don't think so. It's... it's pretty much a constant thing for me. Even when I'm feeling completely fine and my mood is totally normal, I still struggle to keep everything straight. There hasn't really been a time in my life where the disorganization just went away.
Do you often feel restless, like you have trouble sitting still?

Yeah, I do. Um, especially during long design calls for work. I just start feeling this... this pressure building up in my body to get up. So I end up pacing around my office, or I'm constantly shifting from chair to chair, even when I'm really trying to look focused on the screen. It's definitely hard to just sit in one place.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, euphoric, or unusually irritable for several days in a row?

No, I haven't. I mean, I get frustrated sometimes if a project isn't going well, but I've never had a time where I felt unusually high or euphoric for days at a time. My mood is usually pretty steady.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things?

No, not really. I mean, I have normal worries, like hitting a deadline for a software release or just regular day-to-day stuff, but... I wouldn't say it's excessive. I don't really find myself sitting around feeling anxious about a bunch of different things.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

No, not really. My mood has been fine. I don't feel down or... or depressed at all. Like I said, I deal with the usual stress from work, but overall I feel pretty normal in that regard. Nothing that makes me feel sad or low.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a longstanding pattern since childhood of disorganization, losing school materials, forgetting to turn in completed work, and daydreaming, with current impairment across both work and home settings. Hyperactive/restless behavior is also present (pacing, shifting in chair during long calls). Symptoms persist even when mood is normal, and screening in the interview did not support bipolar, depressive, or generalized anxiety explanations. This is most consistent with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation under ICD-10 F90.0.
